provider.name: Generic JSON Lines
provider.organization_type: generic newline-delimited JSON interchange, streaming, logging, bulk-import, archival, and record-oriented data format
provider.description: Generic JSON Lines is a provider-agnostic record format in which each non-empty line contains one complete JSON value, usually an object. It is commonly identified by the extensions .jsonl, .ndjson, .jsonlines, and compressed variants such as .jsonl.gz.
institutional_context: JSON, JSON Schema, Unicode, IANA, and RFC standards

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting JSON Lines and NDJSON format documentation, JSON standards, schema validation, encodings, media types, streaming parsers, database import behavior, cloud ingestion, logging conventions, compression, checksums, security guidance, and licensing metadata.
purpose.authoritative_notice: JSON Lines and NDJSON documentation, RFC 8259, ECMA-404, JSON Schema, IANA, Unicode, and implementation-specific documentation remain authoritative for their respective syntax, media types, encoding, validation, APIs, and behavior.

format_profile.record_boundary: one line terminator separates adjacent JSON values
format_profile.whitespace_handling: Leading and trailing JSON whitespace may be tolerated by parsers, but canonical production should emit exactly one compact JSON value followed by one newline.
notes: Do not confuse JSON Lines with a single top-level JSON array.
Do not confuse newline-delimited JSON with RFC 7464 JSON Text Sequences.
Each line must independently parse as a complete JSON value.
Embedded literal newlines inside strings must be escaped.
Strict JSON parsing should be the default.
Expose permissive modes only through explicit configuration.
Preserve raw lines when troubleshooting malformed records.
Apply backpressure and bounded memory when reading untrusted or very large files.
Emit exactly one JSON value per line.
Never pretty-print records across multiple physical lines.
Use atomic replacement to avoid partial canonical outputs.
Record generator version, schema version, source files, record count, and checksum.
A JSONL file is validated record by record unless a project-specific envelope format is defined.
Use oneOf or a discriminator when multiple record shapes share a file.
Preserve schema identifiers and versions in output manifests.
Compression may prevent efficient random splitting.
Preserve integer precision when consumers use IEEE-754 doubles.
Document date, time, binary, decimal, and identifier conventions explicitly.
The JSONL container format does not determine the license of its records.
Preserve record-level and file-level license metadata independently.
Do not infer rights from file extension, media type, or public availability.
Preserve SPDX expressions, Creative Commons URLs, ODC licenses, source citations, and rights holders.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
JSON Lines and NDJSON terminology, MIME-type usage, implementation behavior, and documentation paths may vary; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not treat a single top-level JSON array as JSONL.
Do not split on newline bytes without respecting UTF-8 decoding and escaped newlines inside strings.
Do not store credentials, API keys, cookies, OAuth tokens, or session identifiers in this JSON file.
Always preserve encoding, schema version, record identifier, source, line number, byte offset, checksum, license, citation, and provenance.
